tldr: The field contribution is a compact exact reference calculus for coherent ordinal attribution across all ordered dose contrasts. For every \(J\ge1\) and \(K\ge2\), adjacent local MITE converts the complete common-law \(D/B/\operatorname{PN}\) surface into \(O(KJ^2)\) triangular entry-exit cells, diagonal and adjacent anchors, and nonnegative mixed differences. Rational acceptance and rejection certificates have quadratic size and polynomial bit complexity, while explicit response-profile enumeration has \(N_{J,K}=\sum_h(K-h){J\choose h}\) columns and is exponential in \(J\) when \(K\ge J+1\). Decomposable gluing, crossing-time transport, ordered-coupling extrema, generic response-profile linear programming, and confidence-region projection remain credited ingredients; exact benchmark counts corroborate but do not prove the calculus.
gap: Binary-treatment MITE identifies an ordinal necessity target, and the general multiarm framework of Hashimoto, Kawakami, and Tian computes sharp bounds with explicitly enumerated response profiles. Ordered coupling and decomposable graphical margins already supply the generic extremal and gluing ingredients. The inspected literature and code do not expose the complete all-dose \(D/B/\operatorname{PN}\) surface as a quadratic-size exact representation, its invertible mixed-difference coordinates, or its rational certificate and bit-complexity contract.
fill: The paper proves the \(O(KJ^2)\) triangular-table representation, the exact profile-count comparison, necessary-and-sufficient mixed-difference membership, polynomial-bit rational acceptance and rejection certificates, the affine benefit and denominator-masked necessity image, and coverage-preserving outer projection.
